title: auth-api-401-429-debug-notes-michael-2026-02-27
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs from recent customer reports of 401s and 429s when calling the hosted API (mostly from mobile clients). Quick notes, commands tried, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary of incidents observed:
- 2026-02-23 09:12 PST: customer A (mobile) reports intermittent 401s for ~10 minutes, then cleared.
- 2026-02-24 14:05 PST: internal load test produced repeated 429s at ~180 rps from a single API key.
- Patterns: 401s usually for a small fraction (2-3%) of requests; 429s concentrated when bursts exceed token-rate rules.

What I tried (commands + outputs):
1) Simple curl auth check (local):
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/redwood/text/generate
   -> 200 OK for valid key, response body OK.
2) Simulated burst with httpie (10 concurrent):
   seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
   -> saw ~15% 429s when concurrency high, headers included: X-RateLimit-Limit: 300, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 3
3) Token rotation check: created new API key in console, used same client -> consistently works. Suggests issue not scope/permissions.

Logs / error snippets (copied):
- 2026-02-24T14:05:12Z ERROR auth-service token validation failed for token id tkn_XXXX: signature mismatch
- 2026-02-24T14:06:20Z WARN rate-limiter quota exceeded for key key_YYYY: window=60s allowed=300 used=301
- Client-side report: "sometimes get 401 then next retry 200"

Hypotheses:
- 401s: could be transient token cache invalidation on edge auth proxies. When auth-service rotated JWKS cache or deployed, a short window of signature mismatch could happen. Also possible clock skew on some mobile clients leading to expired tokens reported as 401.
- 401 alternative: token malformed / truncated by some mobile SDKs when adding header (observed on older Android WebView builds).
- 429s: expected when bursts exceed configured per-key request rate. Some mobile apps retry aggressively with no backoff causing bursts. Also observed single-key fanout from API key sharing (multiple devices using same key).

Evidence supporting each hypothesis:
- JWKS rotation timeline (infra deploys): correlated deploy at 2026-02-24T14:04 which matches 401 spike.
- Rate-limit headers during tests show Remaining=0 and Retry-After set.
- Customer reported they were shipping a client update that switched HTTP library (no backoff).

Quick mitigation steps taken:
- Added temporary jittered backoff to mobile SDK (patch) and asked customer to opt-in to beta.
- Increased visibility: added more logging on auth edge to capture token id + key id for 401s (PII-safe sampling).
- For rate limits: adjusted per-key soft limits in staging to test behavior, and throttled burst traffic at edge for specific customer key.

Observations / gotchas:
- Some 401 logs show token id present but signature mismatch — strongly points at key rotation / cached public key mismatch. Need to verify JWKS propagation across datacenters.
- Mobile clients sometimes double-URL-encode Authorization header when using certain proxy libs; causes header parsing failure and 401.
- Retry patterns: client retries on 401 as if transient and succeeds; on 429 clients should backoff but many do fixed small sleep (100ms) causing thundering herd.

Next investigation steps (owners):
- Infra (Devon): verify JWKS cache TTL and propagation, add metrics for jwks-refresh events.
- SDK (Aisha): add stricter header construction + tests to avoid encoding issues; implement exponential backoff with capped retries.
- Product/Support: reach out to affected customers with recommended SDK patch and request app logs for exact header values when possible.
- SRE: correlate 401 spikes with deploys and edge cache invalidations (search logs between 14:00-14:10 on 2026-02-24).

Longer term fixes to consider:
- Graceful JWKS rotation: publish new key but keep old key valid for 5 minutes and ensure per-edge cache invalidation TTLs align.
- Rate-limit guidance + SDK helpers: client-side rate-limit-aware retry helper with jittered exponential backoff.
- Per-key burst tokens: introduce a small token-bucket burst allowance to absorb short spikes (pay attention to abuse vectors).

Scratchpad: quick curl examples for reproducing 429 with headers (to run locally)
  for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done

Notes to self: capture a sample 401 request raw headers from customer next time (include Proxy, client lib version, OS).

Raw links / refs:
- Rate limit playbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Rate+Limit+Playbook
- Related Jira: INF-4237 (investigate mobile 401s)
- SDK PR with backoff helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1189

-- Michael
